changes.before: Assign score <- 4 and then score <- 9. What value will print(score) display?
changes.after: A variable gives a value a name that you can use again.

before: In R, score <- 3 assigns the value 3 to the name score. The arrow points toward the name receiving the value.
A later score <- 8 changes what score refers to. The name remains the same.
print(score) retrieves and displays the current value. print("score") would display text instead.
These examples use one number at a time. The display label [1] is not part of the number.
Expected result: [1] 8. Follow the instructions in order; this is a worked example, not an in-app execution.
after: A variable gives a value a name that you can use again.
The assignment arrow points toward the name that will hold the value.
Give score the value eight in place of three.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```r
score <- 3
score <- 8
print(score)
```
The output is `[1] 8`. Print reads the latest value of score.
